summary: The bill requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to submit three reports to Congress within 180 days evaluating CBP’s progress implementing a biometric entry-exit system, including effects on wait times and travel, data-matching for departing noncitizens, and information sharing with Canada under the Beyond the Border agreement.

scores.thoughts: The bill requires DHS to produce several evaluation reports on an existing biometric system. It explicitly preserves authority to collect existing user fees but neither authorizes new appropriations nor mandates spending reductions. Any administrative costs for the reports are incidental and minimal.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions relate to health insurance, medical services, or healthcare regulation.
No provisions address firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.

The bill directs evaluation and improvement of CBP’s biometric entry-exit system specifically to enhance identification of visa violators, support counterterrorism, and strengthen border enforcement. This directly advances immigration enforcement objectives.
No provisions relate to reproductive health services or abortion access.
The bill references counterterrorism benefits of the biometric system but does not alter military budgets, force structure, or defense appropriations.
No provisions address environmental regulation, emissions, or conservation.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or entitlement spending.
No provisions address schools, student aid, or education policy.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement priorities for drugs.
The biometric system aids identification of immigration violators, but the bill does not modify criminal sentencing, policing practices, or rehabilitation programs.
The bill requires the system to minimize disruption to legitimate trade and travel, but it does not change tariffs, trade agreements, or protectionist measures.
No provisions address deficits, debt ceilings, or fiscal targets.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid programs.
No provisions address voting access, voter ID, or election administration.

The bill advances a biometric data-collection system and requires privacy protections only for U.S. citizens in one report; overall it supports expanded government biometric use rather than additional privacy safeguards or oversight.
No provisions address worker protections, collective bargaining, or union rights.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
